sent:
Sneak Energy D&D drop — here’s the pointed teardown you asked for, written for a January drinks launch where the page must convert and ads keep learning.

Cut from the drop page
- Global nav, footer catalog links, and any path back to home/range.
- Autoplay/carousel hero; keep motion only if user‑triggered below the fold.
- Secondary CTAs (“Learn more,” “View all,” newsletter signup in hero).
- Early popups; reserve exit‑intent for bounce only.
- Duplicate SKU tiles and long brand story blocks.

Keep/add
- Above‑fold: single promise (what it is, why it’s better), delivered price, primary CTA, review stars + count. If limited, state it in the H1.
- Sticky add‑to‑cart after first scroll.
- Starter bundle locked to the free‑shipping threshold; preselect best‑seller.
- Objection killers (3–4 bullets): taste, sugar/caffeine, servings per pack, delivery/returns.
- Trust row: payments, dispatch ETA, returns policy.

Wireframe (top to bottom)
[Slim logo] [Optional true‑limited timer]
H1: Limited run [or] The [benefit] drink that actually tastes good
Sub: Who it’s for + when to use (one line)
Hero image: in‑hand or pour (no autoplay). Reviews snippet.
Price (incl. delivery)    Primary CTA [Add to cart]
Row: 3 reasons (taste, energy/occasion, servings)
—
Module: Starter bundle (variety + best‑seller preselected) + free‑shipping callout
Module: Social proof (2–3 short quotes)
Module: Ingredients/nutrition highlights (icons, scannable)
FAQs (4): taste, sugar/caffeine, shipping/returns, how many to buy
Footer: legal only
Sticky ATC present after first scroll

First‑week tests (drop‑first)
- Promise order: “Limited run” first vs. “Loved by [x]+” first.
- Hero asset: in‑hand vs. pour shot vs. clean pack on flat color.
- Price framing: delivered price vs. ex‑shipping + threshold note beside CTA.
- Default: variety bundle vs. single‑flavor best‑seller.
- Reviews position: in hero vs. just below fold.
- Sticky ATC: on vs. off.
- Video: lazy‑loaded click‑to‑play vs. muted autoplay below fold.
- Exit‑intent: value content (nutrition/taste) vs. incentive.

Creative refresh (for a skeptic)
- Ship three concepts, each in three variants:
  1) Taste‑first (UGC sip + instant reaction)
  2) Occasion fit (workout, study, late shift — one per ad)
  3) Drop/collectible (limited run, set completion)
- Variant styles: UGC testimonial, founder to‑camera, ASMR pour/closeup.
- Kill‑switch: retire any unit after ~3 weeks of falling CTR; keep anything still climbing. Queue replacements before fatigue.
- Every paid click goes to the drop page, not the homepage.

Decision rule
- Optimise to first orders in week one. Shift budget toward the concepts + audiences producing first orders; away from cheap traffic that does not. Counting right is non‑negotiable.

PS: Sundrift’s site returned a 502 here today. While that’s fixed, ship a lightweight fallback drop page using the wireframe above (one CSS file, no heavy apps) so you can point paid and email to something that loads.

If you want this turned into a one‑page wireframe for Sundrift (copy + sections ready to paste), say and I’ll send it.
